text:
andrew.k: heads-up — saw a steady memory growth in KV cache on long-context perf harness (approx 24h). not an allocation leak per-se, looks like fragmentation + small-block churn. :eyes:

sergei: can you paste the profiler snapshots? rough numbers help.

andrew.k: sure — attaching quick summary: peak Rss +1.3GB over baseline, resident growth correlates with number of continuations, avg free-list bucket skew (small blocks) -> frag ratio ~1.42.

andrew.k: stack trace / sample from heap profiler: 
```
alloc buckets: 16B/32B/64B/128B/256B/512B
most allocations landing in 64B/128B; reclaim is delayed because of KV slab alignment policy.
compaction events are rare (only on OOM attempt).
```

maya: ok that matches what i saw in the stress runs. fragmentation mainly in the 64/128 buckets, re-use rate drops as seq length grows.

taylor: did we change any block-size policy recently? last kernel selection patch changed aligned KV padding to 64B. maybe that pushed more into the 128 bucket.

andrew.k: yes — alignment bumped to 64B for perf reasons. helped throughput (fewer loads) but increased internal fragmentation for certain tokenization patterns.

sergei: options: 1) reduce alignment to 32B (less fragmentation, maybe slower kernels), 2) introduce hybrid-bucketing (split 128 into 96/128 logical buckets with compaction), 3) periodic compaction during idle windows.

andrew.k: proposing a hybrid approach: keep alignment/throughput benefits, but add small-block sub-buckets + lightweight compaction when reuse drops below threshold. sketch config: 
```yaml
kv_allocator:
  base_alignment: 64
  sub_buckets_for_small: [48, 80] # logical sizes to catch 64-96 range
  compaction:
    enabled: true
    reuse_threshold: 0.25 # if reuse rate < 25% over 5m
    cpu_budget_ms_per_min: 50
    max_defer_time_s: 300
```

maya: curious about CPU cost. compaction may spike p99 latency if done on hot threads. need a throttle and prefer background worker pinned to lower priority.

taylor: +1 on background worker. also suggest trying block size tune to 96/192 instead of 128/256 — we should benchmark.

sergei: one more thought — incremental compaction where we move only fully cold slabs (no active KV refs). cheaper and safe. mark-and-evict approach.

andrew.k: agree. plan: prototype hybrid bucket allocator + incremental compaction. tests: 24h long-context harness, compare rss, frag ratio, p50/p99 latency, CPU overhead. if good, canary on dedicated pool with canary-rate=1% and rollback on rss>baseline+500MB or p99 latency +20ms.

maya: add metrics to console: kv.frag_ratio, kv.reuse_rate, kv.compaction_cpu_ms, kv.compaction_moved_bytes. dashboards for rollouts.

taylor: i'll write the microbench and perf harness changes. sergei can you review allocator impl?

sergei: yeah, i'll take a look. also add a flag to force compaction in CI to catch regressions. ci-bot: please add a nightly job for forced compaction runs.

ci-bot: noted. created job: nightly/kv-compaction-smoke (runs at 03:00 UTC).

andrew.k: thanks. i'll start a PR with allocator sketch and perf numbers. rough ETA EOW for prototype. any major objections?

maya: none from me, just monitor cpu/p99 closely.

taylor: no objections. prefer small incremental rollouts.

sergei: SGTM. if prototype looks flaky we can try aggressive bucket coalescing + immediate free merging.

andrew.k: cool — i'll post PR link + initial datapoints here when ready. :thumbsup:
